what: Undo of a root registration compares the snapshot with == instead of !=, so a root that changed since it joined is silently dropped (its changes leave review) while an untouched root is refused.
The no-roots guard tests `run.roots is None` instead of emptiness, so a run with zero roots is no longer refused and gets an empty bundle that can be approved with nothing reviewed.
The known-alias sets are swapped: FINDINGs naming a removed root are accepted, while SUPERSEDES retractions of findings in a removed root are rejected as unknown-alias (contract failure).
Registration is skipped unless the tool check is exactly 'allow', so a write that is put to the person ('ask') lands in a folder never registered as a root and its baseline is missed.
`&&` became `||`: the conversation is compacted on every continuation in an interactive session, and a headless session with compact set tries a refused compaction.

Late-discovered nested repos pick their alias from current roots only, not taken_aliases(), so a retired alias can be reissued, colliding with round history and stall anchors (the sibling call site in _add still uses taken_aliases).
